name: Taimaka (Founders Pledge)
beneficiaries_note: The countries the model's summary names: Nigeria.

missing_data.note: Measured: Taimaka counts the children treated for acute malnutrition, and the treatment's effect is from trials and cohorts of the same community protocol.

summary: Community treatment of acute malnutrition in Gombe State, Nigeria. Founders Pledge's page states a cost of about $70 per child treated; our bridge values a child treated with GiveWell's Taimaka analysis.

sections.title: Founders Pledge's figure
sections.explainer: Founders Pledge's own figures, as its recommendation page states them. It publishes no spreadsheet for this recommendation, so these are the model's only evaluator rows.

sections.title: From children treated to units of value
sections.explainer: charityevals' bridge, not Founders Pledge's: the page gives a cost per child treated but not what a treatment is worth. We value one child treated by Taimaka as GiveWell's 2024 Taimaka analysis does (deaths averted, later income, its downside and excluded-effect adjustments, before its leverage and funging step): its units of value per dollar times its cost per child.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's figure, quoted on its page: Taimaka uses the simplified OptiMA protocol and "they can treat a child for around $70". No sheet is published, and the page doesn't say what the cost covers. High end ours: GiveWell's $105 for Taimaka's scale-up.

source.title: GiveWell, Taimaka malnutrition treatment CEA (2024)
source.note: Main CEA, 'Cost per child treated for malnutrition' (charityevals model taimaka-malnutrition-treatment-2024, row cost_per_child_treated_for_malnutrition)

rows.explainer: GiveWell's cost per child with severe acute malnutrition for Taimaka's 2025–27 scale-up: its annual budget over the children it expects to treat. Founders Pledge's $70 has no stated scope (its footnote cites the OptiMA-DRC trial, which treats moderate and severe cases together); if it covers cheaper, lower-risk moderate cases, this bridge overstates the result, by up to the 1.5× gap between the two costs.

rows.explainer: GiveWell's allowance for what the Nigerian government and other funders would otherwise do: about −10%. Applied with credit by share of resources off, as in GiveWell's own model.

rows.label: GiveWell: Taimaka's share of all spending on the program

source.title: GiveWell, Taimaka malnutrition treatment CEA (2024)
source.note: Taimaka $1,595,995 a year over total expenditure $1,849,633 (with the domestic government's $253,638) (charityevals model taimaka-malnutrition-treatment-2024)

rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources on, Taimaka's money gets its share of the outcome: 86%; the government's spending gets the rest.

rows.label: Units of value per child treated
rows.explainer: GiveWell's value of one child treated, after its leverage and funging step (or, with credit by share of resources on, Taimaka's share of all spending). Almost all of it is deaths averted, and GiveWell values the program's later income gains as a ratio of them, so all of it moves with our value-of-life lever (pinned at 1 in Founders Pledge's view).

rows.label: Units of value per dollar at Founders Pledge's cost
rows.explainer: GiveWell's value of a child treated, over Founders Pledge's cost per child.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: Units of value per dollar, in GiveWell's units (one unit = a year of doubled income for one person). With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
